correctness.summary: Edge IDs start at 1 instead of 2, breaking the e^1 reverse-edge pairing used by DinicMaxFlow; the first forward edge's reverse is written to slot 0 (head sentinel) instead of slot 2, corrupting the residual graph and the min-cut, so the returned profit can be wrong.
correctness.triggeringInput: n=1, profit[0]=10, no prerequisites (prerequisiteHead[0]=0). The source->node0 edge gets edgeId=1, reverse 2; DinicMaxFlow's DinicDfs does flow[1^1=0] instead of flow[2]. Although this trivial case may return totalProfit correctly, any instance with a min-cut on negative-profit nodes mis-augments. E.g. n=2, profit[0]=10, profit[1]=-3, prerequisite edge node0 requires node1.
correctness.rootCause: Same convention violation as MaximumClosureFlow: the library pairs an edge e with its reverse via e^1, which only works when ids start at an even number (Flow.cs uses edgeId=2). Starting at 1 makes 1^1==0 alias the 'no edge' sentinel and leaves the true reverse slot 2 unmaintained.
correctness.suggestedFix: Initialize 'int edgeId = 2;' and grow the stackalloc edge arrays accordingly so the unused index-0/1 slots are accounted for.

perf.summary: newFlow buffer is allocated but the min-cut/selected set is never recovered, and edge arrays at n*6 are a loose bound; right-size and consider dropping unused capacity.
perf.currentCost: Five arrays at stackalloc int[n*6] (~120n bytes stack). The function only returns totalProfit and never reads newFlow after DinicMaxFlow, yet newFlow occupies n*6 ints of stack and is written by Dinic. The n*6 multiplier is a conservative guess unrelated to the actual edge count (n profit edges *2 ids + prerequisite edges *2 ids).
perf.proposedChange: Size edge arrays from the real bound 2*(n + prerequisiteEdgeCount) + 2 (named constant), ideally via a caller-supplied maxEdges. newFlow is required by DinicMaxFlow's signature so it must stay, but its length only needs to cover used edge ids, not n*6. Tightening the multiplier shrinks the hot stack working set.
perf.rationale: Reduces stack footprint and cache pressure during the Dinic run, and removes the risk of under-sizing on dense prerequisite graphs where prerequisite edges exceed 2n. Tighter buffers stay resident in L1/L2 across Dinic's repeated BFS/DFS sweeps.
perf.risk: If prerequisite edge count can exceed 2n, n*6 may currently UNDER-allocate and silently corrupt the stack — verify the documented bound. Switching to a maxEdges parameter is an API change (ergonomics). With a correct fixed bound, behavior is unchanged.
